value.rationale: The exact least singular value is a natural and quantitatively necessary stability invariant for recovering a relative complex phase from three Gabor line profiles. The two-sided mod-one comparison and the exact 2(μ−1) worst-frequency exponent classify line designs into badly approximable, general finite-exponent, and Liouville stability regimes; this informs how rapidly phase recovery deteriorates as carrier separation increases. It is not merely the known yes/no uniqueness result and avoids claiming global noise stability. The phase-frame/Diophantine bridge makes the precise rate mathematically meaningful for rational-versus-irrational measurement geometries.
